details:
ASTROBASE X — Dual-World Mission Survival Simulator

ASTROBASE X is an interactive educational space mission simulator designed to help students understand the challenges of operating a human outpost on the Moon and Mars. It allows users to take the role of a mission commander and make important decisions to keep their simulated crew and outpost safe.

Users can select either the Moon or Mars, start a mission, and manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy, and habitat integrity. During the simulation, they face different mission challenges and unexpected events. Their decisions affect resource availability, crew safety, and overall mission success. At the end, users receive a mission performance report showing their results.

The main benefit of ASTROBASE X is that it makes space exploration more interactive and understandable. Instead of only reading about space missions, students can experience simplified mission-management challenges and learn about resource planning, problem-solving, scientific thinking, and decision-making.

The intended impact is to encourage students to explore planetary science, space technology, and STEM education. It aims to make complex space exploration concepts accessible through an engaging educational experience.

The project is designed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with browser-based technologies such as LocalStorage and JSON for simulation data and progress management.

What makes ASTROBASE X creative is its dual-world approach: one simulation system supports two different planetary environments. The Moon and Mars have separate mission conditions and challenges, while users experience the consequences of their own decisions. The project also emphasizes educational value, realistic visual design, usability, and clear explanations of scientific information.

During development, important factors include scientific accuracy, educational usefulness, user experience, resource-management logic, accessibility, and the distinction between NASA-sourced information and illustrative simulation values. The simulator is an educational model, not a real spacecraft control system.
